ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r3.claim: Because Aaron is addressed alongside Moses, this command came after Moses reached Egypt; Aaron was not with him in the valley of Ṭuwā.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p37/r3.anchor: directive was necessarily given later when Moses (sws) had reached Egypt

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r10.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r10.claim: Although Pharaoh had greatly transgressed, the command to address him gently shows how important method and tone are to successful religious preaching.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:25/r10.anchor: 24 ve 43. âyetlerde Firavun’a uyarıcı gönderilme gerekçesi olarak “onun sınırı çok aştığı” ifade edildiği halde 44. âyette “Yine de ona söyleyeceklerinizi yumuşak bir üslûpla söyleyiniz

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r5.claim: The second command to go supplies the object omitted from the earlier command: Moses and Aaron are to go to Pharaoh with the message.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r5.anchor: ولما حذف من يذهب إليه في الأمر قبله نص عليه في هذا الأمر الثاني. فقيل: اذهبا إلى فرعون أي بالرسالة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r6.claim: A more distant interpretation says the first command sent them to people generally and the second specifically to Pharaoh, so the command is repeated because its destination changes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r6.anchor: وأبعد من ذهب إلى أنهما أمرا بالذهاب أولا إلى الناس وثانيا إلى فرعون، فكرر الأمر بالذهاب لاختلاف المتعلق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r7.claim: Pharaoh is identified as the destination because he transgressed through corruption and claiming divinity and lordship apart from God.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p336/r7.anchor: ونبه على سبب الذهاب إليه بالرسالة من عنده بقوله إنه طغى أي تجاوز الحد في الفساد ودعواه الربوبية والإلهية من دون الله

STUDYQURAN:20:43/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:43/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:43/r1.claim: The command to both Moses and Aaron echoes the command to Moses in 20:24 and is linked with 79:17 and other Moses passages.
STUDYQURAN:20:43/r1.anchor: Cf. the similar wording addressed to Moses in v. 24; 79:17; see also 26:10–11; 27:12; 28:32

TABATABAI:20:41-44/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r11.claim: God renews the command to both messengers, matching the previous joint address and prohibition against slackening.
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r11.anchor: جمعهما في الأمر ثانيا فخاطب موسى وهارون معا وكذلك في النهي الذي قبله

TABATABAI:20:41-44/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r12.claim: Gentle speech forbids harsh and violent treatment and is one of the essential etiquettes of inviting people to faith.
TABATABAI:20:41-44/r12.anchor: المنع من أن يكلماه بخشونة وعنف وهو من أوجب آداب الدعوة

TABRISI:20:40-44/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:40-44/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:40-44/r17.claim: The second command to go to Pharaoh repeats the first for emphasis.

TABRISI:20:40-44/r18.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:40-44/r18.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:40-44/r18.claim: Alternatively, the first command addressed Moses alone, while the second addresses both brothers to make Aaron a prophet and partner in the mission.
TABRISI:20:40-44/r18.anchor: وقيل: إن في الأول خص موسى بالأمر

TABRISI:20:40-44/r19.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:40-44/r19.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:40-44/r19.claim: Pharaoh exceeded the limit in tyranny.

TABRISI:20:44/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:44/r7.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:20:44/r7.claim: One account says Aaron was in Egypt; when Moses was told to come there, God instructed Aaron to meet him, and the brothers conferred and went to Pharaoh.
TABRISI:20:44/r7.anchor: إن هارون كان بمصر فلما أوحى الله تعالى إلى موسى أن يأتي مصر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#2/r1.claim: Repeating the command to go to Pharaoh emphasizes the order.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#2/r1.anchor: {اذهبا إلى فرعون} تكرير الأمر بالذهاب للتأكيد.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#2/r2.claim: The explanation of Pharaoh’s transgression was already given earlier in this sūra.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p408#2/r2.anchor: {إنه طغى} قد مر في هذه السورة

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:41-43/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:41-43/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:41-43/r4.claim: Pharaoh had risen up and become arrogant.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r3.claim: Pharaoh's transgression means that he disbelieved.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p260/r3.anchor: {اذهبا إلى فرعون إنه طغى} [طه: 43] إنه كفر.

QASHANI:20:41-44/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:41-44/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:41-44/r2.claim: Moses is the heart and Aaron the intellect; they must approach the tyrannical commanding soul with God's proofs and remembrance.
QASHANI:20:41-44/r2.anchor: اذهب يا موسى القلب أنت وأخوك العقل

QASHANI:20:41-44/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:41-44/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:41-44/r4.claim: God encourages and protects the heart and intellect in their struggle against the soul's tyranny.
QASHANI:20:41-44/r4.anchor: شجعهما الله بالتأييد والإعانة والمحافظة والكلاءة والإحاطة بما يقاسيانه ويكابدانه منها

SULAMI:v1p445#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p445#3/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p445#3/r1.claim: Inwardly, Pharaoh is the target, but Moses is in truth sent to the magicians: God does not send prophets to His enemies, who have no standing with Him to warrant their mission; rather, He sends them to rescue His believing friends from among enemy disbelievers.
SULAMI:v1p445#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : الإشارة إلى فرعون وهو المبعوث في الحقيقة إلى السحرة ، فإن الله لا يرسل أنبياءه إلى أعداءه ،

SAMIN-DURR:20:43/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:43/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:43/r1.claim: The omitted destination in the earlier command and the explicit Pharaoh here avoid repetition; both journeys target Pharaoh, while بآياتي is stated earlier and omitted here.
SAMIN-DURR:20:43/r1.anchor: الذهابان متوجهان لشيء واحد وهو فرعون، وقد حذف من كل من الذهابين ما أثبته في الآخر

SAMIN-DURR:20:43/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:43/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:43/r2.claim: The suggestion that the first command was to go generally to the people and the second specifically to Pharaoh is unlikely.
SAMIN-DURR:20:43/r2.anchor: وقيل: أمرا أولا بالذهاب لعموم الناس ثم ثانيا لفرعون بخصوصه، وفيه بعد؛

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r1.claim: The command is phrased as a plural imperative addressed to both Moses and Aaron.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r1.anchor: وكذا جمعه في صيغة أمر الحاضر بناء على ذلك أيضا قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r2.claim: Views on Aaron's arrival say God revealed to him in Egypt to meet Moses, inspired him, or that he heard of Moses' approach and went to greet him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r2.anchor: وروى أنه أوحى إلى هرون وهو بمصر أن يتلقى موسى عليهما السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r3.claim: Other possibilities are that Aaron went to Sinai to meet Moses, or that this command came after Moses returned to Egypt and Aaron came out to meet him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r3.anchor: ويحتمل أنه ذهب إلى الطور واجتمعا هناك فخوطبا معا ويحتمل أن هذا الأمر بعد اقبال موسى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r4.claim: One reconciliation with 20:42 says the earlier command did not specify the destination, whereas this one explicitly names Pharaoh.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r4.anchor: بأنه لم يبين هناك من يذهب اليه وبين هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r5.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r5.claim: Another reconciliation says the earlier command concerned the general audience for the mission, while this one directs them to Pharaoh.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r5.anchor: وبعض أخر بأنه أمرا هنا بالذهاب إلى فرعون وكان الأمر هناك بالذهاب إلى عموم أهل الدعوة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r6.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r6.claim: A third distinction is that Aaron was not addressed in the earlier wording but is addressed here.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r6.anchor: وبعض أخر بأنه لم يخاطب هرون هناك وخوطب هنا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r7.claim: A fourth distinction is that the earlier command may send them separately, while this one explicitly sends them together.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r7.anchor: وبعض أخر بأن الأمر هناك بذهاب كل منهما على الأنفراد نصا أو احتمالا والأمر هنا بالذهاب على الاجتماع نصا

ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r8.claim: Al-Alusi finds some proposed distinctions questionable and points to the clear contrast with the first singular command to Moses in 20:24.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p194#2/r8.anchor: ولا يخفى ما في بعض هذه الفروق من النظر والفرق ظاهر بين هذا الأمر والأمر في قوله تعالى اولا خاطابا لموسى

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:43/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:43/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:43/r1.claim: The earlier commission addressed Moses alone, while this one addresses Moses and Aaron, so the wording is not redundant. Aaron may have been told to meet Moses, or may have heard of his approach and gone to meet him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:43/r1.anchor: أمر به أولا موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام وحده وههنا إياه وأخاه فلا تكرير

BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r1.claim: The repeated command is emphatic because the danger is so great that ordinary human nature scarcely accepts the certainty of the order.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r1.anchor: مؤكدا لنفس الذهاب لأنه لشدة الخطر لا يكاد طبع البشر يتحقق جزم الأمر به

BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r2.claim: The reason for the mission is repeated for emphasis and to heighten wonder at Pharaoh’s lack of sense, and at those who follow him.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p20/r2.anchor: من قلة عقله , فكيف بمن تبعه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r2.claim: The particular mission to go was either inferred by Moses from his selection and the signs or explicitly stated but omitted concisely; the reason clause signals it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r3.claim: The reason clause explains the mission: Moses must deliver God's command to turn Pharaoh away from worshipping other than God; Moses accepts and seeks help rather than objecting to fear.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p209/r3.anchor: وإنما صلحت للتعليل لأن المراد ذهاب خاص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p223#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p223#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p223#2/r1.claim: The command returns to the main purpose after the dialogue and explains God's preparation of Moses: He selected him for a great task, sending him with Aaron to Pharaoh.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r1.claim: One reading shifts directly to addressing both brothers; Aaron is already present, having joined Moses by revelation in Goshen, and their fear answers God's command without narrated travel between Horeb and Egypt.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r1.anchor: يجوز أن يكون انتقال إلى خطاب موسى وهارون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r2.claim: Alternatively, the dual command restates the earlier command to Moses and his absent brother; Moses later meets Aaron, tells him, and both then voice their fear. This better fits the sequence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r2.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون جملة اذهبا إلى فرعون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r3.claim: Pharaoh's transgression explains why God commands them to go: their mission is to restrain it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r4.claim: The muṣḥaf writes the final sound with an alif-shaped yāʾ to signal the root طغي, like رضي; a wāw form طغو, like يدعو, is also possible.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p224/r4.anchor: رسم في المصحف آخره ألفا ممالة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287/r1.claim: The repeated command to go to Pharaoh serves for emphasis; its explanation of his transgression is given at 20:24.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p287/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى اذهبا إلى فرعون فائدة تكرار الأمر بالذهاب التوكيد وقد فسرناه قوله ﴿ إنه طغى ﴾ طه 24

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r5.claim: Pharaoh rebelled, became arrogantly defiant toward God, and disobeyed Him.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p294/r5.anchor: أي: تمرد وعتا وتجهرم على الله وعصاه

MUQATIL:20:41-45/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r5.claim: Pharaoh had disobeyed God for four hundred years.
MUQATIL:20:41-45/r5.anchor: يقول: عصى الله، عز وجل، أربعمائة سنة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p55#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p55#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p55#4/r1.claim: The command repeats because the earlier one was unqualified and this one qualified.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r1.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r1.claim: One view says God first addressed Moses alone to honor him, then repeated the order to stress that both brothers must go call Pharaoh.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r1.anchor: فقيل: أمر الله تعالى موسى وهارون في هذه الآية بالنفوذ إلى دعوة فرعون، وخاطب أولا موسى وحده تشريفا له

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r2.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r2.claim: A second view says the repetition shows that one brother going alone would not suffice.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r2.anchor: وقيل: بين بهذا أنه لا يكفي ذهاب أحدهما.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r3.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r3.claim: A third view says the first order concerned going to all people, while this one specifies Pharaoh.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r3.anchor: وقيل: الأول أمر بالذهاب إلى كل الناس، والثاني بالذهاب إلى فرعون.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r13.speaker: الإسرائيليات
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r13.claim: An Israelite report says Moses waited outside Pharaoh's door for a year, unable to find a messenger; Qurṭubī says it consoles later believers facing oppressors.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:43-44/r13.anchor: وروي في الإسرائيليات أن موسى عليه السلام قام على باب فرعون سنة، لا يجد رسولا يبلغ كلاما حتى خرج.

BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r1.speaker: شيخي وسندي
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r1.claim: Bursevī says his spiritual master recounted being commanded in a midmorning dream in Filibe to migrate to Constantinople; after waking, praying, and washing, he left on foot and left his family behind.
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r1.anchor: وسمعت من شيخي وسندي قدس سره أنه نام نومة الضحى يوما في مدينة فلبه

BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r2.speaker: الحافظ
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r2.claim: Hāfiẓ's couplet longs for the day of leaving this station, when companions will ask for news from the beloved's street.
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r2.anchor:
قال الحافظ :
387
خرم آن روزكه زين مرحله بربندم رخت

BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r3.claim: The dual address either uses grammatical predominance or comes after Moses and Aaron have met; the repeated command sets up what follows.
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r3.anchor: هذا الخطاب إما بطريق التغليب أو بعد ملاقاة أحدهما الآخر

BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r4.claim: Pharaoh is a foreign name and title for al-Walīd ibn Muṣʿab; the word generated a verb for acting like Pharaoh, and tyrants are called pharaohs and devils.
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r4.anchor: وفرعون اسم أعجمي لقب الوليد بن مصعب

BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r5.claim: Ṭughyān is exceeding the limit in disobedience; Pharaoh exceeded servitude by claiming divinity.
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r5.anchor: الطغيان مجاوزة الحد في العصيان أي : تجاوز حد العبودية

BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r6.speaker: العرائس
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r6.claim: God sent Moses and Aaron to Pharaoh to cut off his argument and expose the falsehood of his claim; this warns every claimant who lacks proof from God.
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r6.anchor: قال في "العرائس" : أمر الله موسى وهارون عليهما السلام بالذهاب إلى فرعون

BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r7.speaker: العرائس
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r7.claim: Sending prophets to enemies teaches them their inability to guide others or even themselves, like a doctor who cannot treat others and cannot treat himself.
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r7.anchor: والحكمة في إرسال الأنبياء إلى الأعداء ليعرفوا عجزهم عن هداية الخلق إلى الله

BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r8.speaker: العرائس
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r8.claim: The mission teaches prophets that divine election does not arise from worldly causes and should make them grateful; it may also draw prepared believers out from among unbelievers, such as Habib al-Najjar, Pharaoh's relative and wife, and the magicians.
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r8.anchor: وليعلموا أن الاختصاص لا يكون بالأسباب ويشكروا الله بما أنعم عليهم بلطفه

BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r9.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ says Pharaoh was in truth sent to the magicians: God sends prophets to enemies to draw His believing friends out of their midst.
BURSEVI:v5p297#3/r9.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : الإشارة إلى فرعون وهو المبعوث بالحقيقة

RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r14.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r14.claim: Al-Qaffāl explains the repeated command: the earlier wording might mean each should go separately, so the dual command clarifies that both go together.
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r14.anchor: قال القفال فيه وجهان . أحدهما : أن قوله : { اذهب أنت وأخوك بئاياتى } يحتمل أن يكون كل واحد منهما

RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r15.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r15.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r15.claim: Al-Qaffāl’s other explanation is that the earlier command covered Israelites and Pharaoh’s people generally, while this one singles out Pharaoh.
RAZI-FULL:v22p50/r15.anchor: والثاني : أن قوله : { اذهب أنت وأخوك بئاياتى } أمر بالذهاب إلى كل الناس من بني إسرائيل وقوم فرعون

RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r1.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r1.claim: Al-Qaffāl addresses the dual address although Aaron was absent: God spoke to Moses, whose leadership included Aaron, and the dual speech is hypothetical; scripture uses similar collective attribution.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r1.anchor: أن الكلام كان مع موسى عليه السلام وحده إلا أنه كان متبوع هارون فجعل الخطاب معه خطابا مع هارون وكلام هارون على سبيل التقدير

RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r2.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r2.claim: Alternatively, Moses may have paused after God granted his request until he met Aaron, after which God addressed them both.
RAZI-FULL:v22p51/r2.anchor: يحتمل أن الله تعالى لما قال : { قد أوتيت سؤلك ياموسى * موسى } سكت حتى لقي أخاه

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.claim: Nāfiʿ opens the listed first-person yāʾs except ولي فيها and أخي اشدد, where he uses sukūn.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r1.anchor: ففتحهن نافع إلا اثنتين قوله ﴿ ولي فيها مآرب ﴾ وقوله ﴿ أخي اشدد ﴾ فإنه أسكنهما

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.speaker: أبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.claim: Abū ʿAmr uses sukūn on ولي فيها and حشرتني أعمى, opening the other listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r2.anchor: وأسكن أبو عمرو منها اثنتين / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ لم حشرتني أعمى ﴾ وفتح سائرها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.claim: Ibn Kathīr uses sukūn on ولي فيها، ويسر لي أمري، لذكري إن، على عيني إذ, and برأسي إني; he opens the rest.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r3.anchor: وأسكن ابن كثير منها خمسا / ولى فيها مئارب / و ﴿ ويسر لي أمري ﴾ و ﴿ لذكري إن ﴾

IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي، ابن عامر، عاصم عن أبي بكر
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.claim: These readers use sukūn on all listed first-person yāʾs.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p426/r4.anchor: وأسكنها كلها حمزة والكسائى وابن عامر وعاصم فى رواية أبى بكر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p214/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p214/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p214/r10.claim: The commentary explains Pharaoh's transgression as intoxication from divine overpowering, the attribute of the commanding soul; intoxication of divine gentleness belongs to the spirit and produces ecstatic utterances and claims of selfhood.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p214/r10.anchor: جاوز الحد فى المعصية حتى ادعى الربوبية وذلك أثر سكر القهر الذى هو وصف النفس الأمارة ويقابله سكر اللطف وهو وصف الروح

ALUSI-FULL:v16p214/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p214/r11.speaker: قالوا
ALUSI-FULL:v16p214/r11.claim: Some excuse the ecstatic utterance of an intoxicated mystic such as al-Ḥallāj, while those jealous for God say there is no difference between him and Pharaoh.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p214/r11.anchor: قالوا : وصاحبه معذور وإلا لم يكن فرق
